speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the history. Given your age, outdoor activities, and diabetes, are these lesions new or long-standing, and do they appear as scaly patches, open sores, or raised nodules? Additionally, have you noticed any changes in sensation, such as numbness or tingling, in that area?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is The presence of a rough, scaly, sandpaper-like plaque on the left dorsal hand. I also have No tenderness, No pain.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Actinic Keratosis

The description of a rough, sandpaper-like plaque on the dorsal hand of a 65-year-old with significant sun exposure is highly characteristic of actinic keratosis. Given your history of diabetes, I also want to rule out other possibilities like pyoderma gangrenosum or a neoplasm, so I will request a skin biopsy for confirmation. REQUEST TEST: Skin_Biopsy
